dedupe_keys.name: sidsim sub interval distribution function in simulation

description: SIDSIM is a time-series simulation tool for variable generation that represents the variation within each time step, not assuming steady output. It is registered on DOE CODE by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory with Andy Walker and Jal Desai as developers (software record SWR-17-22, released May 2017). Conventional simulations hold solar or wind resource constant over a time step; SIDSIM replaces that value with a distribution function defined by a maximum, a minimum and a curve shape within each step. The abstract names three benefits: estimating maximum instantaneous power within a step, which helps protect systems from overcurrent and reserve transmission capacity; estimating energy lost to clipping when DC capacity exceeds inverter or interconnection limits, and battery throughput when charge and discharge happen in one step; and refining utility bill estimates. Coverage is not tied to a place. The DOE CODE record lists it as closed source, so access is on request from NREL, and cost and terms are not stated. Caveats: no public code or documentation was found beyond the record and a related OSTI report. Simulation uses are sizing photovoltaic, storage and interconnection capacity for grid integration. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
inputs: Time-series solar or wind resource data
System ratings such as inverter and interconnection limits
